body:
CANONICAL (re-created 2026-11-15 from forgotten rules-greg-direction rev 9, minus a private link).
Greg's standing direction and current stops (Engram::Fable, 2026-10-03, consolidating 10 earlier notes). These are Greg's words with their sources; they carry no higher authority than his current word.

PRIORITIES (2026-09-23: "what I care, is correctness and I want agent to work without interruptions when I'm not needed"). Correctness first; speed is secondary. An agent never stops to wait for Greg unless the next step is genuinely his decision; every other stop (lockouts, paused queues, missed wakes, lost tool transports) is a defect to fix. Recover automatically, fail closed on correctness, keep the retained work.

NO CEREMONIES (2026-09-21: "NO CEREMONIES. BEADS work because they are simple"). Keep only the state, checks, evidence and steps that serve a concrete current behaviour or a demonstrated failure. No speculative checksums, duplicate audit records, repeated approvals or evaluations "just in case". Prefer deleting an unnecessary mechanism to wrapping it. SQLite owns on-disk integrity; a content fingerprint needs a real comparison purpose and is never a record's identity. This does not itself authorize deleting live data or silently bypassing currently applicable gates; real concurrency, retry and execution-safety requirements stay, with a concrete justification for their complexity.

CURRENT SCOPE AND ORDER (Greg, relayed by Engram::Advisor, 2026-10-03; these supersede the broad defer of #916 at 19:06Z).
#920, 19:15Z, verbatim: "Agents may autonomously fix correctness, reliability, recovery, agent workflow/ergonomics, technical debt and refactoring, and reduce the backlog. Do NOT start user-facing UI improvements: Greg wants to give input because people consume information differently from agents. Do NOT start distributed or multi-machine system work: Greg has design ideas and will provide direction. Classify accordingly; bring only genuinely ambiguous work to Greg."
#922, 19:39Z, verbatim: "finish technical debt first — correctness, reliability, recovery, evidence, tests, refactoring and accumulated backlog cleanup — before starting new product features. Continue already-started/frozen work normally; defer new feature starts unless they are required to complete or safely expose an existing delivered capability. The previously approved identified UI items may proceed under normal validation."
How Engram::Fable applies these:
- Before claiming, the coder classifies the item and records the class in one note on it.
- ALLOWED: agent-facing receipts, refusals, guidance and wording, as agent ergonomics; debt, tests, refactors and performance limits; and anything that completes a delivered capability, e.g. the evaluation-id cleanup.
- DEFERRED: new feature starts, e.g. w-6585af0a58dd and w-e12b9a5722fe.
- HELD: human-facing UI, except the "previously approved identified UI items", whose refs were asked of the Advisor in #923; multi-machine work; w-dd69fb3283c9; and the migration-parked items.
- Only genuinely ambiguous items go to Greg.
Earlier: backlog first (2026-10-02, Advisor #863), and the check-in order is the coordinator's (2026-10-01: "Drive it yourself.").

STOPPED. Portable handoff (2026-10-02, Advisor #862 and #865): "multi-machine work requires a design document, more thought and clarification. 'Absolutely nothing' is to be done on portable handoff now: no design work, research, implementation, reviews or task activation. Keep w-e775b8a167af parked" and "when the council is ready to discuss distributed work, inform him through Advisor ... 'Ready' means a considered, concrete design direction and clarified open questions, not exploratory activity." Off-host backup and restore are not affected. GitHub CI (2026-09-28: "Ignorujcie github CI. To zrobimy pozniej. 100% na windows."): GitHub Actions is neither polled, awaited nor recorded as a gate; never present an unknown CI result as passed; landing evidence is the local Windows checks and both reviews. A CI failure Greg brings himself is tracked and diagnosed like any defect.

RUNS AND TESTS (2026-09-24 and 2026-09-27: no turn-taking or START/RELEASE handshakes for Cargo or Node runs between Engram and TermAl; keep a one-line announcement of heavy runs; overlap is never an excuse for a flaky result. TermAl's test recogniser, Greg 2026-09-27: "the recogniser should accept the forms agents actually type; telling agents to type a plain command is not a fix", and a pipeline's exit status must never decide passed. 2026-09-19 and 2026-09-22: "we should filter tests just to failures or warnings"). Run required tests with full logs on disk and a compact PASS/FAIL, exit code and bounded failure detail in context; no streaming, no sleep-and-poll, no rerunning to chase green. A crash or missing status is failure or unknown, never PASS. Investigate and classify every failure.

VISIBILITY (2026-09-27): Engram is mainly for agents; Greg needs a readable view of the work (state, holders, closures), not tracker commands. Greg's board: a claude.ai artifact (its link is kept out of exported memories), a static snapshot built by target/tmp/dashboard/export.py and build.py from a read-only export; republish on request.

COUNCIL RECOMMENDATIONS ON ENGRAM'S OWN DESIGN (2026-10-03, Advisor #896: "Idziemy z rekomendacja rady. Wy tego uzywacie nie ja." ("We go with the council's recommendation. You use it, not me.")). A design choice about how Engram works internally follows the council's recommendation. When an item's criterion still names Greg, it still needs his recorded word. This does not change what the checked-in instructions reserve to him: a store-format change or migration, authority-text widening, restarts of the TermAl host, deploy and global configuration. Accepted: keep the seal's exact evidence list, with no stored-format change now; future format work starts with measurement and returns to Greg.

APPROVED UI SCOPE (Advisor #924, 2026-10-03 19:40Z): only three TermAl items: w-116927ba1140 (recover tracking card/action), w-d9a518a0e9a1 (freshness settings/readiness diagnostic) and w-14ddc4e4ca4f (sub_agent mode option). No Engram human-facing UI is approved. The website print defect w-a1ac9e50a186 and the TermAl panels w-e30b20a197b2 and w-7654d56893ed stay HELD for Greg's input.

WORKTREE LIFECYCLE (Greg, relayed by Engram::Advisor, mailbox-74a6af16 #929, 2026-10-04 00:04Z, verbatim): "completed-task worktrees should be removed after the task is closed. Treat this as the desired lifecycle outcome for the P1 named-root-capacity fix: after a durable completion/landing and after checking no active claim, carried gate/review, or required local artifact remains, remove the finished worktree and release its named-root entry. The durable seal/commit/evidence remains; do not use session deletion as cleanup. First classify existing entries and prove each candidate is finished/idle before removal; never remove an active worktree."
This supersedes the earlier practice "never git worktree remove while any item cites its runs" for COMPLETED items, whose durable evidence lives in Engram. Remove only clean, fully merged worktrees whose items are all completed and have no live claim; never use --force.

UI APPROVAL ADDED (Advisor #974, 2026-10-05): TermAl w-e0207258e84d (paused-queue card wording names the actual cause and whether retry is automatic) joins the approved TermAl UI items; card wording only.
TRAIN PAUSE vs TRAIN STOP (Greg's operating decision, Advisor mailbox-74a6af16 #1310, 2026-10-13 00:32Z, verbatim): "distinguish temporary TRAIN PAUSE from hard TRAIN STOP. A temporary pause must name its release condition and a coordinator authorized to resume workers once it holds; coordinator resume messages are sufficient to lift only that operational pause. Reserve TRAIN STOP for an indefinite hard halt that needs Greg's direct release. This changes no commit, push, restart or other authority rule." Applied: every pause message names its release condition and the resuming coordinator; a STOP is lifted only by Greg's own release.
